testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in how long?
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, wait for air pressure to reach 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems. This takes about 45 seconds.

questions.question: If you do not drain the tanks in an air brake system, what can happen?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure
Too much air collects in the system

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure
questions.explanation: Air tanks must be drained to remove water and oil. If water builds up and freezes in cold weather, it can cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: If brake pads rub against brake drums and create too much heat, what happens?

options.text: The brakes will become extra sensitive
The air compressor will turn on to cool the brakes

questions.explanation: When brakes get too hot, they become less effective and can stop working. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: What is true about vehicles with dual air brake systems?

options.text: They keep full air pressure in the brake system when the engine is off
They keep some air pressure in the brake system when the engine is off
The engine must run to build enough air pressure for brakes to work
They do not need time to build air pressure before driving

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine must run to build enough air pressure for brakes to work
questions.explanation: Before driving, you must let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary brake systems.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) uses what color light to warn that the system is not working?
questions.explanation: ABS warning lights are yellow. If the ABS is not working, you still have regular braking power.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, what is the maximum air leak for a triple combination vehicle with air brakes in one minute?
questions.explanation: For a triple combination vehicle, air should leak no more than 5 psi in one minute. If it leaks faster, the vehicle needs repairs before driving.

questions.question: What brake system includes the brake pedal?
questions.explanation: The service brake system works when you press the brake pedal while driving normally.

questions.question: What type of air brake system do most heavy-duty vehicles use?
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: How often should you drain air tanks that have manual drains?
questions.explanation: Drain manual air tank drains at the end of each driving day to remove water and oil buildup.

questions.question: Where is the safety relief valve usually located?
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve is located in the first air tank that receives air from the compressor.

questions.question: What does the application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
The temperature of air in the braking system.
The pressure of air from the compressor.
How many times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: The application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes in an air brake system. Not all vehicles with air brakes have this gauge.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, what happens after air pressure is lost and spring brakes engage?

options.text: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time.
You can continue driving normally with the spring brakes.
The air tanks will automatically refill to a safe pressure level.

questions.correctAnswerText: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with dual parking control valves have a separate air tank that can temporarily release the spring brakes if they engage due to low air pressure. Pressing the correct control will release the spring brakes for a short time, letting the driver move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: For a vehicle with air brakes, how should the air compressor drive belt be before each drive?
questions.explanation: Before each drive, check the air compressor drive belt on vehicles with air brakes. The belt should be tight and in good condition.

questions.question: How is water and oil removed from the bottom of an air storage tank?

options.text: The water and oil are siphoned out.
A drain valve is opened to remove them.
They are removed automatically when the brakes are used.
A sponge is used to soak them up.

questions.correctAnswerText: A drain valve is opened to remove them.
questions.explanation: Water and oil are removed from air storage tanks by opening a drain valve. These must be removed because they damage the brakes. Manually operated tanks should be drained every day.

questions.question: When checking brakes, how much should a slack adjuster move from the push rod?
questions.explanation: Check each slack adjuster by pulling it. It should not move more than about one inch from the push rod. If it moves more than one inch, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: When should a low air pressure warning signal turn on?

options.text: When tank pressure drops below 120 psi.
When tank pressure drops below 55 psi.
When tank pressure drops below 10 psi.
When tank pressure drops below 5 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: When tank pressure drops below 55 psi.
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning signal must turn on when air pressure in the tanks drops below 55 psi. The warning can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: What color are ABS malfunction lamps?
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) malfunction lamps are yellow.

questions.question: What happens when you press the brake pedal in an air brake system?

options.text: The low pressure warning light turns on.
The low pressure warning light turns off.

questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal in an air brake system, air pressure activates an electric switch that turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, what minimum pressure must build up in both systems?
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: What should drivers do with a front brake limiting valve for normal stopping power?

options.text: Set the control to the off position.
Keep the control at the halfway mark.

questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings. To ensure normal stopping power, leave the control in the "normal" position.

questions.question: While driving, spring brakes are held in place by:
questions.explanation: Spring brakes are held in place by air pressure while driving. If air pressure drops low enough, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: When you push down the brake pedal, air brakes work:

options.text: Only if it is warm outside.

questions.explanation: Air brakes do not work instantly because air takes time to travel through the brake lines. There is usually a delay of at least half a second between when you press the brake pedal and when the brakes start working.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle is:
questions.explanation: Know the safe air loss rate for your vehicle. A triple combination vehicle should not lose more than 6 psi per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: The air storage tanks:

options.text: Hold only enough air for one braking cycle.
Hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor stops.
Do not hold air unless there is an emergency.
Hold enough air for more than 1,000 braking cycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor stops.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold enough air for the brakes to work several times even if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: When using the controlled braking method in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Apply the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Apply the brakes with about half of your normal force.
Apply the brakes until the wheels lock.
Apply the brakes with minimal pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: For controlled braking in an emergency, press the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Keep steering movements small while braking this way.
